questions.question: <div style=\"text-align:justify\">Which of the following conditions regarding a chemical process ensures its spontaneity at all temperature ?<\/div>$\n$

**Question Explanation:
$ The$ question asks which combination of enthalpy change (ΔH) and entropy change (ΔS) guarantees a spontaneous reaction at all temperatures.
$ $**Mathematical Calculation:

$ $
    $ $
  • **Option 1 (ΔH > 0, ΔS < 0): ΔG = (+) – T(–) = (+) + T(+) = Always positive. Not spontaneous at any temperature.
    • $ $
  • **Option 2 (ΔH < 0, ΔS > 0): ΔG = (–) – T(+) = Always negative. Spontaneous at all temperatures.
    • $ $
  • **Option 3 (ΔH < 0, ΔS < 0): ΔG = (–) – T(–) = (–) + T(+). Spontaneous at low temperatures, non-spontaneous at high temperatures.
    • $ $
  • **Option 4 (ΔH > 0, ΔS > 0): ΔG = (+) – T(+). Spontaneous at high temperatures, non-spontaneous at low temperatures.
    • $ $
$ $
**Final Answer: (B)
$ $
